*Numbers sources:* CPS and FoodAPS values are the dedup-certified v1 results
in `docs/validation/question_counts.json`. AHS values are the v2 rollup in
`v2/report/v2_report_numbers_collected.json` (`ahs` block). Reproducibility
figures are from the v2 confirmation run (`v2/report/v2_results_report.qmd`).
Nothing here is computed in prose except ratios of cited counts, each shown
with numerator and denominator.

## Scope

Three source surveys have been scored for harmonization against ACS as the
anchor: CPS and FoodAPS in the v1 analysis (subsequently confirmed by the
v2 reproducibility run), and AHS net-new in v2. The unit throughout is the
unique question, not the question pair. A question counts as having a
harmonization path if at least one of its pairs against ACS was rated F1
(direct recode) or F2 (statistical adjustment).

These three surveys carry different evidential weight and this report does
not pool them. CPS and FoodAPS results are dual-generation validated: two
independent model ensembles, one generation apart, reproduce the discard
floor at 97 percent and agree on candidacy at 88 to 91 percent. AHS results
come from a single model generation with no independent check, and are
leads rather than findings. A pooled percentage across all three would
put 744 unvalidated AHS questions into the same denominator as validated
results and is deliberately not reported.

## The funnel, per survey

Every rate depends on which denominator is chosen, so both are shown. The
instrument denominator is every question the survey asks. The
entered-pairing denominator is questions whose subtopics gave them any ACS
territory to be compared against; the shortfall between the two is content
with no ACS counterpart at all.

| | CPS | FoodAPS | AHS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| questions in instrument | 211 | 462 | 744 |
| entered pairing vs ACS | 157 | 118 | 744 |
| share of instrument entering | 74.4% | 25.5% | 100% |
| produced no pairs (no shared subtopic) | 0 | 0 | 263 |
| at least one F1/F2 path | 86 | 56 | 92 |
| reach, of entered | 54.8% | 47.5% | 12.4% |
| reach, of instrument | 40.8% | 12.1% | 12.4% |
| provenance | v1, v2-confirmed | v1, v2-confirmed | v2 only, unvalidated |

The pairing-stage accounting differs by design generation. In v1, questions
with no shared ACS subtopic were filtered before pairing, so CPS and
FoodAPS enter-pairing counts already exclude them. In v2, all in-map AHS
questions entered and the 263 with no shared subtopic surface as an
explicit bucket. The instrument-denominator rows are the comparable ones.

## Tier composition of questions with a path

Each question is assigned its best tier across all of its pairs: F1 if any
pair is a direct recode, otherwise F2 if any pair needs only statistical
adjustment, otherwise F3.

| best tier | CPS | FoodAPS | AHS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| F1 direct recode | 32 | 19 | pending |
| F2 statistical adjustment | 54 | 37 | pending |
| F3 only (no path, but compared) | 71 | 62 | 389 |
| never compared (no shared subtopic) | 54 | 344 | 263 |

The two AHS cells marked pending require a one-line count against
`ahs_candidates.csv` on WORK (best feasibility per unique question over the
92 candidates); the rollup reports pair-level counts (71 F1 pairs, 59 F2
pairs) which are a different unit and are not substitutes. The CPS and
FoodAPS never-compared rows are the instrument count minus entered-pairing
count (211 minus 157; 462 minus 118).

## Combined result for the validated pair (CPS + FoodAPS only)

For the two validated surveys, the combined question-level result is: 275
unique questions compared, 142 (51.6 percent) with at least one path, of
which 51 (18.5 percent) are best-tier F1 and 91 (33.1 percent) best-tier
F2; 133 (48.4 percent) are F3 throughout. On the ACS side, 48 of 115 ACS
questions (41.7 percent) serve as targets for at least one source
question, and 15 serve both CPS and FoodAPS simultaneously. No ACS-side
participation figure exists yet for AHS.

## What the three surveys say together

The pattern across the three is not one number but a gradient in how much
of each survey lives on ACS territory. CPS is three-quarters ACS-adjacent
and harmonizes at the highest rate. FoodAPS is a specialized instrument
where only a quarter of the content can even be compared, but that quarter
harmonizes nearly as well as CPS. AHS enters in full yet reaches only 12
percent, because its bulk is housing-structure detail far deeper than
anything ACS asks, and 263 of its questions have no ACS territory at all.
Where AHS does touch ACS ground, the touch is close: its demographic
questions reach 66 percent, in line with the validated surveys. The
consistent story is that harmonization reach is a property of shared
conceptual territory, not of the survey as a whole, and each instrument's
unique content is exactly the enrichment it offers the others.

## Caveats

AHS figures are single-generation and unvalidated; treat the 92 candidates
as leads. The CPS and FoodAPS tier splits predate the v2 run and reflect
v1 final classifications; the v2 confirmation showed v2 is the stricter
rater on candidacy, so a v2-final tier split would likely be smaller. The
never-compared rows for CPS and FoodAPS are derived by subtraction and
inherit the v1 pairing-stage filter definition. Reach percentages use
denominators shown in the same table; no percentage in this document mixes
units.
